holidays.name: National Deep Dish Pizza Day
holidays.description: A day for Chicago-style pizza fans to dig into a thick, cheesy, sauce-on-top pie that needs a fork, a knife, and a nap afterward.
holidays.origin: Deep dish pizza is widely credited to Chicago in the 1940s, with Pizzeria Uno often named as the birthplace. The food holiday grew out of the internet-era trend of giving every beloved dish its own calendar day.
holidays.funFact: A deep dish pizza can take 30 to 45 minutes to bake, so Chicago pizzerias often ask customers to order ahead while they wait.

holidays.name: National Caramel Day
holidays.description: A sweet and sticky celebration of caramel in candies, sauces, popcorn, and desserts.
holidays.origin: Caramel dates back centuries, with sugar cooking techniques developing in Europe and the Middle East. This unofficial food holiday was created to honor the treat's rich, buttery flavor.
holidays.funFact: Caramelization starts at roughly 320°F (160°C), when sugar molecules break down and recombine into hundreds of new flavor compounds.

holidays.name: Go for Broke Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to taking a big risk, going all in, and giving something your absolute best shot, ideally with a little common sense attached.
holidays.origin: The phrase 'go for broke' became widely known in the 20th century and was famously used as the motto of the Japanese American 442nd Regimental Combat Team in World War II. The observance encourages people to be bold and fearless.
holidays.funFact: The 442nd Regimental Combat Team became one of the most decorated units in U.S. military history for its size and length of service.

holidays.name: Read a Road Map Day
holidays.description: A cheerful rebellion against GPS, inviting people to unfold a paper map, get slightly lost, and rediscover the lost art of navigating without a talking phone.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance appeared as a nostalgic nod to the days before smartphones and satellite navigation, when glove compartments were crammed with folded maps that no one could refold correctly.
holidays.funFact: Folding a paper road map back along its original creases is famously difficult, and many people remain convinced that maps were designed to defy refolding.

holidays.name: National Raisin and Spice Bar Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the humble, cinnamon-scented raisin and spice bar, a treat that tastes like grandma's kitchen on a rainy afternoon.
holidays.origin: Spiced fruit bars have long been a staple of home baking, especially in American recipes passed down through generations. The holiday was created to give this cozy dessert its moment in the spotlight.
holidays.funFact: Raisins are simply dried grapes, and it takes about four pounds of fresh grapes to make one pound of raisins.
